propositions: ProviderSession is constructed 173 lines before the try/finally guard, so provider resolution and client-building code between construction and the guard can raise and leak an opened httpx client.
ProviderSession.__enter__/__exit__ already exist but are never used, and the providers.py docstring describes a `with ProviderSession(cfg)` caller in run() that does not actually exist.
run() should wrap provider resolution through call and teardown in a `with ProviderSession(cfg)` block and drop the now-redundant finally close to avoid double-close.
The fail-closed assert_gated security check must remain ahead of provider construction so no client is opened before the refusal path runs.
A close that raises must still be logged and never propagated, preserving best-effort teardown semantics.
Tests must verify the client is closed when the pre-call window raises and closed exactly once on the happy path.
